title: Shopping
subtitle: trolley, checkout, special offer, refund
summary: Talk about supermarkets, shopping centres and street markets, and say what happens when you take something back.

lesson.heading: In a supermarket
lesson.text: You carry a few things in a **basket** and a lot of things in a **trolley**. You take them from the **shelves** and pay at the **checkout**. The **entrance** is the place where you go into the shop.

examples.text: I only need milk and bread, so I'll take a **basket**.
The most expensive **items** are on the middle **shelves**.
examples.note: an item is a single thing

examples.text: There was a long **queue** at the **checkout**.
examples.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

lesson.heading: How supermarkets make us spend more
lesson.text: Supermarkets put **fresh** bread near the **entrance**, because the lovely smell **makes** us feel hungry. They also move things to different places, so we spend more time in the store.

examples.text: The bread is **fresh** - it has just been made.
The smell **makes** us feel hungry, and hungry shoppers spend more.
examples.note: make somebody feel = cause them to feel

examples.text: Sweets and chocolate are near the **checkout**, so it is easy to add a bar to your **basket**.
You are more **likely** to see the expensive items in the middle.
examples.note: likely to do something = you will probably do it

lesson.heading: Special offers
lesson.text: A **special offer** is a cheaper price than normal, for example three for the price of two. Be careful: people often buy more than they need and then **throw** half of it **away**.

examples.text: There's a **special offer** on melons - buy one, get one free!
I often buy bananas but forget to eat them, so I have to **throw** them **away**.

lesson.heading: Shopping centres
lesson.text: A **shopping centre** is a large covered shopping area. Everything is **under one roof**, which is **convenient** (practical and easy to use), and there is a wide **range** of shops.

examples.text: I like shopping centres because everything is **under one roof**.

examples.note: range = different things of the same type

examples.text: If there is anything wrong with it, the shop will **replace** it.
examples.note: replace = exchange it for another one
a refund = money paid back to you when you return something

lesson.heading: Street markets
lesson.text: In a street market you buy from **stalls**. Many people like the **atmosphere** - the feeling you get in a place. Food and clothes are usually cheaper, and you can try to agree a lower price. This is called **haggling**.

examples.text: I love the **atmosphere** you get from the different **stalls**.
Sometimes you can **haggle** for a lower price.
If you don't like what you buy in a street market, you can't normally take it back and get a **refund**.

lesson.heading: Words and their meanings
rows: a line of people who are waiting
different things of the same type
the feeling in a place or situation

lesson.text: A shop can **replace** a faulty item (give you a new one) or give you a **refund** (give you your money back).

exercises.statement: If you have a lot of things to buy, you need a basket.
exercises.explanation: False. If you have a lot of things to buy, you need a trolley.

exercises.statement: The checkout is where you pay for things.
exercises.explanation: Correct. You pay at the checkout.

exercises.statement: Expensive items are on the top shelves.
exercises.explanation: False. Expensive items are on the middle shelves, where you are more likely to see them.

exercises.statement: If something is fresh, it has just been made.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Fresh means just made or just cooked.

exercises.statement: It's always a good idea to buy things on special offer.
exercises.explanation: False. Sometimes you buy more than you need and throw some of it away.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: a small shop in a street market
the place where you go in

exercises.prompt: I took the shoes back to the shop, but they wouldn't give me a ___ .
exercises.explanation: A refund is money that is paid back to you when you return something.

exercises.prompt: It ___ me angry when shops refuse to give you a refund.
exercises.explanation: Make somebody + adjective = cause them to feel something.

exercises.prompt: When I got to the checkout, there was a long ___ of people waiting.
exercises.explanation: A queue is a line of people who are waiting for something.

exercises.prompt: There's a special ___ on melons - buy one, get one free!
exercises.explanation: A special offer is a cheaper price than normal.

exercises.prompt: I like that supermarket because they have a wide ___ of meat and cheese.
exercises.explanation: A wide range = many different things of the same type.

exercises.prompt: In my local street market there's a really nice ___: it's busy, but everyone is friendly and there's lots of colour.
exercises.explanation: The atmosphere is the feeling you get in a place or situation.

exercises.prompt: I am more ___ to buy something if it's a special offer, because it seems cheaper.
exercises.explanation: If you are likely to do something, you will probably do it.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence about a street market.
exercises.answer: You can try to agree a lower price at a stall.
exercises.explanation: Agreeing a lower price in a market is called haggling.
